utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case number IT-01-48-PT, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Will both parties make their appearances? Prosecution first, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, good afternoon, counsel. For the Prosecution appear Ms. Marie Tuma, trial attorney on my right-hand side, Mr. Hasan Younis, OTP trial support and myself Ekkehard Withopf, acting senior trial attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence, please? Can I have the appearances for the Defence, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bakir Caglar, Mr. President, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And if you could introduce your colleagues, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that he will introduce himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my name is Ahmed Hodzic, and I will possibly be the counsel for Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KREHO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am Dijana Kreho, assistant to the Defence in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the fourth Status Conference held in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Although the accused, under provisional release, is not required to attend the Status Conference, I ordered the accused, Mr. Halilovic, to attend this Status Conference because of the substantial delays arising from the frequent changes of Defence counsel. This matter still remains an issue. There are a number of matters that need to be considered, but I think the first and foremost question will be where are we now in terms of Defence counsel? A letter dated 16th of January, 2003, from Mr. Halilovic to the Registrar requests that the new Defence counsel be Mr. Ahmed Hodzic, with Mr. Caglar as co-counsel. However, in a motion filed on 21st of January, 2003, Mr. Caglar suggests that he shall continue to represent Mr. Halilovic for a period not exceeding 30 days after the replacement is assigned, and it is my understanding that the Registry is appointing counsel as requested by the accused. Having said that, can I hear from Mr. Caglar first on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I shall be brief. I have no intention to waste too much of your time. I have -- I will touch upon three matters -- three issues which to my mind seem relevant. First, in my letter of the 30th of December, requesting the Registry -- to the Registry, in this request I said that I would modify my request in the interests of justice, to -- with due respect to ethical rules by which all the lawyers need to abide by and for that reason, I will not go into details or discuss the matter with the Prosecution, and respond to Prosecution's comments. Secondly, I fully agree with the Prosecutor, with my learned friend, with regard to the fact that the accused is entitled to a fair trial and an expeditious trial. As the Prosecutor -- as the Prosecutor says, and I will quote him, if the Defence is not ready to provide adequate defence, if it speaks of complete, that the Defence counsel lacks professional attitude and responsibility, and therefore the counsel should withdraw from this assignment. Such allegations draw the attention to the reliability of lawyers and bring into question the equality of arms in a case. The withdrawal of a counsel will not cause any significant delay in this case, since Mr. Ahmed Hodzic is the one whom the accused wishes to have appointed as his counsel. As far as I'm concerned, I have to tell you that an enormous amount of work has been done in preparation of the Defence's pre-trial brief. So that is ready. There is also investigation being conducted on the ground. I have acquainted myself with the terrorism of a new kind on the basis of the files of the two previous counsel, new testimony has -- could affect, could influence the further unfolding of this trial, and we shall communicate that to our learned friends shortly. So that they -- Defence counsel will not be entering uncharted ground. Mr. Hodzic, according to what he has told me, is quite ready to take over the exhibits provided by the Prosecution, to fill in the loopholes which still exist in the case. He is quite ready to receive them, to receive this documentation in his office in Sarajevo. Among the measures which the Defence was planning to use in order to facilitate communication amongst the members of the Defence team was the presence, the efficient and effective presence, of a certified interpreter who was, and until recent -- finally we have the contribution of an interpreter and that was one of the missing links until recently but this problem has been solved by now. And thirdly and finally, and here I have the great -- I think I will make the Prosecutor happy when I pronounce mea culpa. I took over the work that was started by previous Defence counsel. I had to invest precious time, including two visits in Sarajevo, to redress a catastrophic situation and try to make up for the damage done. The Prosecution talks about the disqualification of the previous counsel so that the accused could have an adequate Defence. To my mind, it is a good solution, to have a different Defence. This was the solution which was suggested by the Prosecution and he also indicated that the Registry would also -- could also appoint a new counsel in order to make up for the weaknesses existent so far. A lawyer, a self-respecting lawyer, also will do that regardless of what the Prosecution has to say about this. To build up a file, the collection of information and facts are no doubt of primary importance in the Anglo-Saxon system. That I accept. But it also requires that a legal basis, a legal framework, legal foundations to be laid, for people who would be familiar with the truth it has to be -- the jurisprudence of the Tribunal also has to become to be one of the matters to be studied, and it is from the point of view of the continental law that the Defence has indicated in its request that it was ready to cooperate in the preparation of the Defence pre-trial brief, and that is that. And that is what I have to tell you, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Quite regrettable to hear that but before we move on, frankly, I couldn't follow this phrase when you mentioned the previous counsel, mentioning the new terrorism or the new evidences which will affect the future trial. Could you clarify that a little bit more?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President. I merely wished to say that one had to bear in mind the humane sociological and historical dimension of this case. One had to decipher the dramatic experience, and that is why I used the terminology which was perhaps slightly ambiguous, because we were talking about terrorism which has not been known in Europe before the war in ex-Yugoslavia, and I therefore tried to understand those people and their mindset, their way of thinking, their -- the way in which they expressed themselves. And for that reason, I had to go into this case in depth. I had to study it in depth, and not only to collect some testimonies or check certain facts. I also had to understand men and that is what I tried to do. My education, my training, forces me to do that, and I had to go through this very dramatic recent history and it is owing to this new knowledge that we were able to come to new testimonies, to very disturbing facts. The Prosecutor -- and we shall deliver, disclose these to the Prosecutor tonight or tomorrow. That is what I wish to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's enough. Before we move on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to other matters, at this moment I want to comment on the Prosecution's attitude towards Mr. Caglar briefly. I think it is one thing to comment on the lack of cooperation on the part of the Defence counsel, but quite another to question his professional competence. In the future, the Prosecution should bear in mind that the Court will not welcome such strong or inappropriate and unnecessary comments. Is there anything you would like to add at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are a number of issues the Prosecution wishes to raise and the Prosecutor, the Prosecution will avoid to make any comments on the professional competency of professor, Dr. Caglar. The issue of assignment of Defence counsel, unfortunately since meanwhile one year, one complete year, is the main issue in this case, and it's the main issue that significantly delays proceedings, although the Prosecution has timely filed its pre-trial brief eight months ago in June of last year, and it has done everything, everything to speed up the proceedings, the Defence case or the preparation of the Defence side, appears to be not much advanced. More to the contrary, it appears to be in a very embryonic state, and it appears to be in a very embryonic state because we have a very, very unique situation on the Defence side which gives serious raise to concerns. In particular, since this case is an important one for the Tribunal, and it could be tried within a reasonably short term, the Prosecutor already indicated that the presentation of its case would probably last for three months only. In order to understand the situation, it is necessary, and I think this is key to make an informed and a right decision, on the further assignment of Defence counsel, that the Prosecutor -- that the Prosecution is allowed to briefly recapitulate the core events regarding the assignment of Defence counsel in this case. It is necessary, since -- and that I really want to emphasise -- Mr. Hodzic is now the fifth -- the fifth Defence counsel the accused wishes to have assigned within a short period of time, namely eight months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me, how is it fifth?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: It has first been Mr. Balijagic, then it has been Mr. Soyer, then Mr. Halilovic, the accused, wanted -- requested to have assigned, Mr. Kreho, that was the third one, Mr. Caglar was assigned as the fourth one, and now he's nominating Mr. Hodzic as the fifth one. I repeat that, the fifth one within eight months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Kreho was never appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: He was never appointed, however within 8 months, for Defence counsel. In September 2001, Mr. Balijagic already mentioned at the request of the accused has assigned. In February 2002 we already got to know from Mr. Balijagic that there is a possibility that he may withdraw at a later point in time. In March last year, Mr. Balijagic indicated, and I'm quoting, "That any change in the composition of the Defence team of the accused would not lead to any delay in the preparation of the case." In April, the Pre-Trial Judge during one of the Status Conferences, asked Mr. Balijagic to confirm whether it is likely that he would withdraw. In April, 2002, again, the Pre-Trial Judge ordered the parties to file their Pre-Trial briefs, the Prosecution in June 2002, the Defence in September 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Withopf, sorry to interrupt you but do we have to explore all the facts of the past to find out cause and effects of everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I think it's quite important to explore these facts since we have a situation, Your Honour, a situation since one year, that Defence counsel for the accused and the accused himself are telling us there will be no delay, and we have a delay since eight months, the period to file -- the deadline to file the Defence pre-trial brief has been -- has been extended twice over the last half a year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And I have a serious concern, the Prosecution has a serious concern that it will again not be possible for any successor of Mr. Caglar to file the Defence pre-trial brief in time, what means Monday next week. That's the current deadline. The Prosecution has serious doubts as to whether this will be possible and the Prosecutor thinks in the interests of justice, and the Prosecution is only making a recommendation, the Prosecution doesn't request it formally but it makes a recommendation to not assign Mr. Hodzic as the successor or to not direct the Registrar to assign Mr. Hodzic as the successor of Mr. Caglar but to direct the Registrar to assign the Defence counsel who has proven before trial proceedings in this Tribunal that he or she is able to provide a proper and a speedy defence to the accused. Again, this is a case that could be tried within a very short period of time. It's not a big case. But it is an important case for the Tribunal. And the Prosecution understands and based on the fact that it never or normally doesn't interfere with the assignment of Defence counsel by Registrar, does understand that in this particular case, there needs to be a clear direction from the Pre-Trial Judge or from the Trial Chamber in the interests of justice. The interests of justice means also an expeditious trial. This is finally in the interest of the accused as well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you clarify the reason why the Prosecution recommends the Registry not to assign Mr. Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I can easily clarify this. This material, Your Honour, this is the material the Prosecutor tried, and I emphasise tried, to disclose two and a half months ago, this is all the material that is key for the preparation of the Defence in this case. The Prosecution understands, and Mr. Caglar was repeatedly complaining about this fact, that Defence hasn't these materials to their disposal. How can Defence file a pre-trial brief without having ever read all the materials that are key, that are crucial, to the preparation of the Defence? We still don't know whether Mr. Hodzic is able to read English. I assume Mr. Hodzic's native language is Bosnian-Croatian-Serbian language. We don't know whether he will actually be able to read all these materials that are key for the preparation of this case. I think that's a question that should be asked, keeping in mind the memorandum that has recently been filed by the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Frankly, I couldn't follow in full. Was there any fault on the part of Mr. Hodzic for belated disclosure of those materials?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Certainly not, and the Prosecution wishes to again emphasise that all comments are certainly not related and are not directed to the person of Mr. Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So a major concern on the part of the Prosecutor is a language barrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's the main concern, and another concern is the period of time that has passed in the past without the Defence being able to read the materials that are key for the preparation of the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Since this is some extraordinary circumstances, and having heard what has been said, I wonder if Mr. Halilovic has anything to say in regard -- with regard to the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the main reason for which I am here, and I'm grateful to you for having invited me to attend this Status Conference, and I also hope that at the end of this Status Conference we will have an answer to the question as to whether I have the right to a defence, because my rights to a fair and correct defence have been threatened and reduced to a minimum. I can't exactly say who has infringed my rights, whether the lawyer, the Registrar, or some third party, but 17 months have passed since the indictment was submitted. I still don't have a Defence team provided for by the rules from the International Court of Justice. Please understand, and I want to be quite clear about this matter, this is not the result of capricious behaviour on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. my part. It's the result of the fact that my requests were not granted and I think that I have the right, right to a defence on the basis of the rules from the international court. And naturally this is a logical thought and I think that these rules should in no way damage my rights because I'm now in a situation which is totally new to me. Up until this time, up until this case, I never even had to pay a parking fine or anything of that kind. My first lawyer, Faruk Balijagic, I have to say I'm surprised by this because I didn't know that in February, March and April, he announced that he would be withdrawing from the case. I requested that an objection be raised in relation to the indictment, that a foreign lawyer be appointed as co-counsel, someone who was well acquainted with Anglo-Saxon law, and I requested that other conditions be ensured to make sure that I could work properly, administrative assistants, office space, et cetera. The Prosecutor says that this is not a big case. I think it's a very big case. And I think it requires two or three investigators and assistants for the Defence, because a translator because most of the documents we receive is in English and then it's translated a few months later into Bosnian. When I was allowed to -- provisional release, I appointed two experts who have compiled eight reports and they've all been provided to the Prosecution, but these experts still have not been recorded, put on the record but the Registry and I think this is for banal shortcomings on the part of the lawyer. Before coming to this Status Conference I spoke to Mr. Balijagic I asked him why he didn't object -- why he hadn't objected to the indictment because I wanted to state something about it here and ask the Trial Chamber to ensure that I didn't suffer because of what the lawyers had failed to do. His explanation was that he didn't object to the indictment, as he said, because of operations which were in course with the Prosecution, and also because he had reached an agreement with the Prosecution according to which the indictment would be withdrawn at a given moment in time. And this agreement, Balijagic said, is an agreement he reached with the chief Prosecutor, Carla Del Ponte. This is something he stated in front of witnesses on several occasions. As far as other Defence issues are concerned, he told me, after I had insisted, that he form a Defence team, he told me that the Registry had told him that this was not an urgent matter, and at the beginning they had received from two investigators, they had -- but then they withdrew the investigators so a lot of material has remained, in addition to what the Prosecution has proposed, there is a lot of -- there are a lot of documents that remain because the investigator simply doesn't have sufficient time. The translator recorded is someone who no one knows, the translator suggested by the Registry is someone who is not known by anyone from the Defence team. It's a woman who lives in Mostar, not in Sarajevo, and nothing has been translated for the Defence apart from perhaps a letter that Mr. Balijagic sent to the Prosecution. I was also told that this kind of defence team, the kind of team that I suggested and I think that I have the right to such a defence team, he said that such a team might be authorised in the second stage of the proceedings but not before. So the Defence has one investigator at the moment, one assistant, and that is all. Translation, technical processing of documents, office material, one big and two small computers, and all other expenses, expenses that I have to bear. It's true that Mr. Balijagic promised that he would deal with certain debts that had to be settled with translators and this amounts to something between 6.000 and 7.000 euros. This is a promise he made a year ago. After Mr. Balijagic withdrew from the team, the Registry did not accept Mr. Kreho as defence. It's not true that I suggested Dijana Kreho be appointed. I suggested Mr. Kreho be appointed as lead counsel. The Registry, without having consulted me, refused to appoint Senad Kreho, and appointed Mr. Soyer. I would like to clearly state, I would like to apologise for an impolite letter that I addressed to Mr. Soyer but that correspondence with Mr. Soyer lasted for too long in the Defence's opinion. I'm sorry, perhaps Mr. Soyer is an excellent lawyer but I don't know Mr. Soyer and if I have the right to a defence, then I should be in a position to express what my position is, and not to have Defence counsel appointed without being consulted about this. We commenced to work with Mr. Caglar, but his opinion was that the files from the Ministry of the Interior should be looked into, files from the AID, the secret police, the cantonal court and Prosecution, and the archives of the Republic of Croatia. He considered that all these -- all this material should be consulted. This work was all carried out by a small team, one investigator, one Defence assistant, together with me. We had to write in the Bosnian and then translate that into English, send it to Mr. Caglar to translate it into French. This represented additional costs and it took up a significant amount of time. A month ago, when I asked Mr. Hodzic to help me, and he accepted to do so, and when I informed Mr. Caglar about this, professor Caglar suggested that Mr. Hodzic, as an experienced and military lawyer, should be appointed as lead counsel and that he, professor Caglar, should remain as part of the Defence team and should be co-counsel. So my suggestion is what I -- is the assertion I made in the letter dated the 16th of January, if you're asking me for my opinion, and finally, I would request that a Defence team be finally formed because one could say that I have in a way been penalised even before the commencement of the proceedings. That's all I have to say. Thank you very much. And thank you once more for having invited me to this conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'd like to point out one thing, Mr. Halilovic, since the issue was raised, the right of the accused to choose a counsel of his own is -- should be respected, according to the Statute and Rules. However, in cases of counsels appointed by the Tribunal, it is not without any limit, as was noticed in previous decisions regarding Defence counsel issue. In case of Mr. Kreho, it was noted that there had been some conflict of interest, and all the other decisions were legitimately done by the Registrar or by the Chamber. Having said that, so your intention is to have Mr. Hodzic as your lead counsel, with Mr. Caglar remaining as co-counsel. Thank you. And it is Mr. Caglar's intention, however, to withdraw from the case. Can I hear from Mr. Caglar? Yes, you may sit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to say I have no choice. I have never dropped someone on -- I've never dropped someone I decided to defend, never let anyone down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you like to add anything, Mr. Withopf? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour there are a few issues that need to be clarified. The first and the main issue is the alleged agreement between the Prosecutor and the accused and/or his Defence that the Prosecution would withdraw the indictment against the accused. To make it very clear, the Prosecution never intended and does not intend to withdraw the indictment against the accused. The second issue I just want to stress to get the facts completely right. First Defence counsel, Mr. Balijagic, the accused actually cancelled his power of attorney, as we all know, and to get a second thing right, the accused, for a period of time, that extended three months, did not communicate with assigned Defence counsel, namely Mr. Soyer. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The Registry will look into the matter and will decide whether Mr. Hodzic is fully qualified to be appointed as a lead counsel, and that will be done in due course. Apart from these matters, there are a lot of issues to be dealt with today. On matters of Defence team, am I correct in understanding that the parties, especially the Defence, received an informational memorandum from the Registry explaining what the Registry can provide in terms of interpretation or -- translation assistance during the pre-trial Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. I wasn't informed, not officially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that will be done in due course. In short, to a certain extent, a translation and interpretation service will be provided by the Registry. Let's deal with some disclosure matters and some other matters. My understanding is that a lot of materials already have been disclosed to Mr. Caglar or former counsel, the 66(A)(i) materials and exhibits and some interviews, interview materials of the accused. Where are they now? Who has what documents? Could you clarify that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my office, Your Honour. I'd like to add that the documents that were provided to me by Mr. Soyer and at a much later date by Mr. Balijagic, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Withopf?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is actually a serious issue the Prosecution wants to use this opportunity to raise this again. The Prosecution made available as a courtesy copy taking into account the difficulties Mr. Caglar was facing in respect to not getting materials from Mr. Balijagic, provided on 4th and 5th December, in the context of the last Rule 65 ter meeting, these materials. This is a courtesy copy, produced by the Prosecution. This courtesy copy involves huge materials, and I really wish to have the opportunity to detail this. That involves transcripts in both English and B/C/S of the lengthy interview of the accused. This involves 25 video tapes of such an interview, three further video tapes, 123 witness statements in B/C/S, 197 witness statements in English, additional six witness statements in French, three audiotapes, two CDs containing crime scene photographs. Two further audiotapes, five transcripts of further witness interviews, more than 115 documents, quite a number of such materials are actually Rule 68 material that the Prosecutor put together in fulfilling its obligation under Rule 68. On 5th -- or 4th December, after the Rule 65 ter meeting, the Prosecution asked Mr. Caglar to wait for a few minutes to give the Prosecutor an opportunity to take the materials down, an interpreter has been provided. Mr. Caglar disappeared after 20 minutes without giving an explanation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Withopf, I have to interrupt. We don't have to go back to all those issues. You made the point and I understand the frustration of the Prosecution to make all the courtesy -- photocopies but we have to admit there were some problems in practically speaking a language barrier for Mr. Caglar so let's put aside those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Okay. I'm more than happy to put such issues aside but I want to stress and to emphasise that to date the Defence doesn't have such materials. It's offered again. And I would suggest to us, actually Mr. Hodzic, whether he will be able to file the Defence pre-trial brief on Monday week thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will get to the matter later on. Let me deal with the reciprocal disclosure matter first. Just a second. Yes, Mr. Caglar?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. President. I don't have the ability to read into the -- to read the Prosecutor's mind, what I'm interested in is to contribute to the efficiency of this trial, to ensure that the proceedings are conducted in a correct manner. This matter has already been discussed. I cannot have -- I wasn't able to have all these documents because I didn't have the necessary team. This is not a matter that concerns one man alone. The Prosecutor provided, disclosed a courtesy copy of all these documents. Obviously I am not an orchestra, I'm not a team. I can't do everything alone. I need a team that has to be formed in order to carry out this work. I can't do it alone. I've done everything that was possible for me to do alone, to an extent I succeeded and to an extent I failed. That's all I have to say, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let me get back -- go back to the issue of reciprocal disclosure a minute. Mr. Balijagic, former counsel, formally triggered the reciprocal disclosure obligations of Rule 66(B) and 67(C) and this was adopted by Mr. Caglar at the Status Conference in October, 2002. My understanding is that the -- some arrangements were made for Mr. Caglar to inspect the so-called Seve files and the state surveillance files at the OTP in December last year. I would like to hear the positions regarding this matter. What happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very briefly, the statement is completely correct, both the Seve files and the state surveillance files have been made available for Mr. Caglar for inspection, pursuant to Rule 66(B). Such an inspection happened on the 4th and on the 5th December last year. The Prosecutor again agreed to provide Mr. Caglar with a courtesy copy of quite a number of documents he wanted to have copied, a number of such copies have been provided on the 5th of December last year and additional material, additional copies, again courtesy copies, are ready to be disclosed today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having heard so far that -- let's go directly to the issue of pre-trial brief on the part of Defence. When will we finally get to see the Defence pre-trial brief? As Mr. Withopf suggested -- indicated, the Prosecution's pre-trial brief was filed more than a half a year ago, in June last year. Can we still expect to see the Defence's brief on or before 17th February, next Monday, the result of an extension that I granted? Could you make any observation on that, Mr. Caglar?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that depends on the appointment of new counsel obviously but as a matter of principle, I am really sorry to have to say this, but at the moment, and I am really sorry to have to say this, but we will require one month to finish the work that we have started. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The one month time frame, was it discussed with the lead counsel to be, that is Mr. Hodzic, Mr. Caglar?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I had an exchange of opinions with Mr. Hodzic last night, and we agree. We fully agree with that. Of course, if that is agreeable to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That is only when Mr. Hodzic is appointed by the Registrar as the lead counsel? If I'm right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we set the deadline for the pre-trial brief apart for a while and let's deal with some Prosecution's matters for a minute first. The JNA military expert, manual, what is the current position, or current status regarding that matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the relevant portions of such manuals have been fully translated. The military expert is about to provide the Prosecution with his final report. The external military expert for the Prosecution. And such materials are amongst the disclosure materials that have been offered in the past and will be offered today again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What did you refer to when you said the final report?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have indicated in the last Rule 65 ter meeting that the external military expert witness for the Prosecution is in a position to provide the Prosecution with his final draft of his written expert opinion by end of January. Such a draft has actually been submitted. Recently there are a few issues that need further clarification. The military expert is currently working on such issues and he has promised that we would get his final report, that will then be filed within the next few weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What about the translations?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Translations of the manuals?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Translation of the manual in B/C/S into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Again, that's already done, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And the final report will be translated again?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Into B/C/S language?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Yes, it will be translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When do you think it will be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: It mainly depends when the military expert will submit his final report. Then it's a matter of translation only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Since the Prosecution is saying that it has a brief look on that final -- on the report, will there be an addendum or amendment to the Prosecution's pre-trial brief?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: As it stands now, there will be no amendment to the pre-trial brief based on this written report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then what do you think about setting a deadline for disclosure of that expert military report?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: If the deadline is reasonable and takes into account the delay of the filing of the Defence pre-trial brief, the Prosecution would suggest eight weeks and there wouldn't be any problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What would you respond -- how would you respond if the Defence will say that in order to produce a -- its pre-trial brief, it has to look at those military expert report?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I would respond as follows: It's a quite unusual situation, the Defence at the time it has to produce its pre-trial brief is actually in possession of the written expert's opinion of the Prosecution. That's a quite unusual situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And what is the status of the Prosecution's expert in pathology who performed the -- the pathologist who performed some post-mortem reports?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The Prosecution is happy to announce that such pathologist reports have been fully translated, the materials will be amongst the materials that can be offered for disclosure today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I note the -- on 5th of February this year, the Prosecution filed a motion to add four witnesses to its list, the statements of these witnesses were disclosed, as I understood it, to Mr. Caglar in October of last year?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I hear the Defence's response to this at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These testimonies.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We are sorry, the microphone is switched off. We cannot hear the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received these statements some seven or eight days ago, end of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Legally speaking, the Defence has some more days to respond to this motion of the Prosecution, so you can take time. Since Mr. Caglar has said so, can I expect that to see the Defence's pre-trial brief in a month's time from now? That is around end of March? Before the end of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And Mr. Withopf, could you try to disclose the expert report until the end of March?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: We certainly will try to do so. And the Prosecution is very optimistic that it will be able to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. And 92 bis witnesses? I understand that statements of 43 witnesses are expected to be tendered for admission under Rule 92 bis, and were available, I understand, all the certified statements of these witnesses were disclosed, with the Prosecution's pre-trial brief. I would recommend the parties to have a word on that and to reach an agreement on the admission of these statements. Is there any progress -- has there been any progress on that matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: As Your Honour mentioned, almost all -- I have to correct this -- almost all Rule 92 bis witness statements have been disclosed out of 45 are disclosed actually are all of them. However, out of 45 witness statements, the Prosecution got 43 certifications pursuant to Rule 92 bis. Two additional ones are still needed and the Prosecution will get such certifications as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. One more thing is related to Rule 68 disclosure. What is the position in terms of those materials? And also I understand that the Prosecution has sought some assistance from the Defence in identifying key areas of interest, search criteria. What is the status? Could you brief me on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Actually, the Prosecution would be very happy if it would have some assistance by the Defence. Such assistance has been announced several times. However, never, ever the Prosecution got such an assistance. The Rule 68 system-wide search is ongoing. The Prosecution is using a wide range of key words. It has asked several times the Defence to provide the Prosecution with additional search criteria. As I already mentioned, never ever got a response to such a request. It is ongoing today, we will be able to again disclose additional Rule 68 materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Caglar, do you have any say on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'd like to point out that whether the Defence is offering some search criteria or not, the Prosecution is duty-bound still to disclose whatever material they have in their custody. In terms of exhibits, I understand there are some bundle of documents named "Sarajevo collection" provided by the Bosnian authorities from the official archives and the Prosecution stated that it may be used to form part of the exhibits. What is the current status?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Again, there is not much of a change as compared to the last Status Conference. The Prosecution is working on the basis that it will finally produce 200 to 300 exhibits, the analysis of the documents that result from the Sarajevo collection is currently ongoing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. If the Registrar has a calendar -- thank you. Looking into the calendar of next month I notice -- I note that the 24th, Monday, is around -- is Monday. So if Mr. Caglar and the Defence team could file the pre-trial brief on or before that date. There will be a month -- 40 days from now, around.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And this time, I'm making it simply clear that there will be no more extensions. And the Prosecution, if the Prosecution could disclose the military expert report until on or about the third -- a week Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. after, Monday, the 31st of March?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution will do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And major concern of the Prosecution on the qualification of Mr. Hodzic, is in the language barrier problem. I don't see that there would be many obstacles for the Registry to appoint Mr. Hodzic but it's a matter for the Registry, so that is -- that matter is to be seen, and is there any issues to be raised at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution wishes to ask Defence counsel whether Defence is actually able to get handed over such materials today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Caglar?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAGLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already said it, Mr. President. Tonight or tomorrow morning. I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the next Status Conference will need to be held by 10th of June, while the next 65 ter conference presided by our senior legal officer should be held from mid-to-late March. Initially in my first Status Conference we are looking at the end of June, 2002, last year, as for when the case would be ready for trial. Now it is February, 2003, and I want this case ready for trial by the end of April at least. If there is nothing remains, Mr. Halilovic, is there anything you would like to add at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe just a brief comment and a small request. As a matter of fact, I'd not discussed with the Prosecutor the withdrawal of the indictment. If something was done in this regard, it was done by lawyer Balijagic. I had nothing to do with it. I did not take part in any discussions about the withdrawal of the indictment nor do I know anything about it. Secondly, I hope you will accept my proposal concerning the assignment of the lawyer and appointment of interpreters and investigators because without that, it simply won't be possible to work. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That matter will be looked into. Then this Status Conference is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
